correctness.rationale: Published Kaneko–Stoll Theorems 2.1–2.2 bound the entire infinite search to two finite product families, with exactly 13 and 231 candidate products. Independent exhaustive product-first and factor-first exact integer code was executed; the former tests 5523 divisors, the latter 3672 unordered admissible pairs, and both return the same seven pairs. The exclusion of weight one is proved by parity and minimum factor size. The algorithms and outputs are embedded as standalone files.

value.rationale: Complete sharp classification of a natural symmetric lowest-complexity sparse-product Diophantine regime, determining all weight<=3 products of odd three-bit factors and exact maximum 1029. Motivated directly by the 2021 paper’s explicitly posed existence question for weight triples; the modest finite classification is not arbitrary or a reformulated general bound. It supplies an exact benchmark for the multiplicative carry phenomenon.
